verifiers_claim_audit.claim_exact: End to end: 150 Harbor tasks that grade a live service and had failed every rollout under the previous order, 2 rollouts each, with the same harness (current nano-rlm, no service API) under this branch. 88% of rollouts pass, and 147 of the 150 tasks pass at least once. Rollouts that kept the service as a background job pass 93% (176 of 190). Rollouts that only started it with `nohup` or `&` inside a command pass 48% (15 of 31): that process is still killed when its command returns, which PrimeIntellect-ai/nano-rlm#229 addresses.
missing_for_independent_audit: sampling, seeds, budgets and repetitions baseline
subgroup classification for remaining planned rollouts
public raw E2E archive or result URL
verifiers_claim_audit.limitation: No raw E2E link found in the bounded PR body, complete one-page issue/review comments/reviews, companion PR body/issue comments and current-head workflow artifact metadata. This does not prove no raw data exists elsewhere.
denominator_caveats: 150 x 2 implies 300 planned rollouts; no raw valid-rollout manifest was read.
The stated subgroup totals 190 and 31 do not specify all planned rollouts or establish disjoint/exhaustive membership.
147/150 is task-level at-least-one success, distinct from per-rollout pass rate.
Tasks selected for previous universal failure do not establish general benchmark improvement.

h1_restored_proposals.claim: Indexed recurrent KDA honors token index strides, sizes separate output states per flattened token, and avoids state writes when state output is disabled. CUDA and Ascend paths are changed.
implementation_reading: CUDA initial/final index loads multiply i_t by stride_indices_tok.
Separate final_state allocation uses B*T instead of sequence count N when ssm_state_indices is supplied, protecting per-token storage bounds.
Continuous-batching writes additionally require STORE_FINAL_STATE, preserving a borrowed initial state pool when output is disabled.
Ascend uses corresponding per-token allocation and block-pointer boundary checks plus ascend_compile_kwargs; present-head Ascend runtime remains an author-disclosed gap.
h1_restored_proposals.memory_implication: Correct storage can require MORE allocated memory (B*T state records rather than N). No lower-memory benefit is established; preserving aliased pools and correct state capacity precedes allocation optimization.
h1_restored_proposals.tests_read: 48 parametrized indexed cases span dense/packed, state orientations, stride1/2, accepted token1/2, in-place/separate/disabled output; compare naive outputs/states, untouched pool slots, returned shapes and resumed decoding. Tests not executed locally.

limitations: Synthetic random inference-only banks and one seeded shared query. No real activations, learned pseudo-query, training/backward, model quality, GPU or upstream AttnRes implementation is measured.

Inputs are prepacked once in the parent. Worker timing excludes fixture generation, quantization, input loading and output persistence; these costs are recorded separately. This is not per-step quantization or a deployable activation/retention system.
Every method/case/repeat uses a fresh Python process. Int8 workers load only packed values, scales and query, never the dense float bank. No memory mapping is used.

Process peak is an OS lifetime high-water resident/working-set measurement sampled after output persistence, before final metadata serialization/exit. It includes Python/NumPy imports, input buffers, allocator behavior, temporaries and output storage; it is not precise operator-only allocation or GPU peak memory.

Post-import and post-load high-water increments are differences between lifetime maxima, not isolated operator peaks. Freed or cached allocations, page residency, OS scheduling and system load affect observations.

Linux uses procfs VmHWM/VmRSS in KiB converted to bytes; ru_maxrss is retained only as a diagnostic. If procfs is unavailable, the fallback ru_maxrss can contain an inherited pre-exec high-water and current RSS is unavailable. Darwin ru_maxrss uses bytes. Windows uses GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize and WorkingSetSize in bytes.

The full-int8 path retains packed inputs and creates a complete float32 dequantized bank before the existing full_mix; construction/quantization was excluded. The tiled path makes two passes, recomputes RMSNorm/logits, and accumulates weighted sums in float64. No latency or memory improvement threshold is assumed.

Worker order is deterministically shuffled within each shape/seed to interleave methods and repeats. This reduces simple fixed-order bias but does not control temperature, background work or OS allocator differences. At most three repeats are descriptive, not statistical performance guarantees.

Fixture/output and code/config hashes identify numerical evidence. The stable result hash excludes timing, memory, process IDs and platform scheduling; the full observation hash includes variable measurements. Exact numerical hashes can differ across NumPy/platform versions even when tolerance checks pass.
